problems_found: sanitize.drop_combos leaked credentials. A URL password with an empty user was kept ('redis://:password@host'), because the email pass ran first and the userinfo pattern needed a non-empty user. Passwords containing '@' survived in both URL and bare forms ('bob:p@ss@host'). 'user:pw@<IP>' was kept because 'user' counts as a label prefix.

drop_combos also damaged IOCs. It cut the port and path from 'https://user@host:8443/path', 'postgres://u:p@db:5432/app' and 'ssh://git@host:22/x', and it collapsed git scp remotes and ';'-separated address lists.

drop_combos was open to ReDoS. It runs on every string of every module result, hostile pages included. The unbounded '\b<scheme>*://' pattern was quadratic on runs like 'a-a-a-...' (about 1 s per 40k characters, so minutes on pages several MB long). The first rewrite of the bare user:pass pattern also hung on 'a:b@' runs; this was found while testing the fix and then fixed.

sanitize_result left combos in several places: dict keys, res.error, source_statuses reasons, Finding.key (which is stored by to_dict), and entity values of non-URL pivots. A pivot that the scrub left invalid was never dropped.
Engine.run_module built ctx outside its try block, so a PolicyError or ConfigError raised while building the run's context escaped run_module, although the contract says run_module never raises.
Partial-result recovery (_pick_result) could fall back to a ModuleResult built for another entity, or by another module, and give its facts to the subject entity.

If a module marked its result BLOCKED or RATE_LIMITED and then hit Cancelled, RequestCapReached or QuotaExceeded, the recovered result was rewritten to ok/empty. That turns 'could not verify' into 'nothing found', which breaks rule 5.
Findings appended directly to res.findings could share a deterministic id. Overrides, feedback and sightings are keyed by these ids (AR09).

The engine never set Runtime.in_scan, so the AR10 rule that datasets over 5 MB are not downloaded during a scan (enforced in WP04's DataStore) never took effect. A cancel_reason left over from an earlier scan labelled the stop reasons of the next one.
When the global timeout expired, the scan loop exited without calling the kill switch, so runs still in flight kept sending requests.
The interim TLP:RED gate looked only at options.tlp. A seed marked RED through options.seed_tlp did not keep third-party modules away.
Team rule 7 was not enforced: a module whose provider publishes submitted lookups would still receive the value when selected with -M, --all-modules or `v3lum run`.

Evidence files had several problems. They were written without passing the redactor, so a configured key inside res.raw reached disk (AR01). The file name contained the raw entity value, such as an e-mail or CPF (A4/AR24). The module name was used unsanitised in the path. A case_id passed to investigate was not validated, so a caller could write outside the cases directory.
Contract-violation messages (strict-mode exceptions and lenient-mode log lines) quoted module-supplied URLs without redaction, keys included.

correlate had three faults. RULE_ERRORS entries were overwritten, so an invalid rule id or severity error disappeared once an ATT&CK error was recorded. ATT&CK ids that rules set on Correlations at run time were never validated (P301 cond 6). check_fixture compared the error message before and after the run, so a second fixture failing with the same message passed silently.
The 'at most +1' upgrade cap lived in an in-memory flag, so a finding that was stored, reloaded and upgraded again went up two levels (P322 cond 5).

Smaller defects: Graph.to_dict dropped findings, so from_dict(to_dict()) lost them. Provider timestamps in epoch milliseconds were silently dropped. ModuleResult.from_dict crashed on a null pivot confidence. Keep paths for nested lists ('rows[][]') were rejected. Credential-like keys (api_key, secret, authorization, private_key, cvv) were not in the second net.

open_issues: Deviation from the spec, based on evidence: 'awswaf' was listed as a strong (any-status) marker, but the real research sample of portaldatransparencia.gov.br (a default-on BR source) is a normal HTTP 200 page that embeds the AWS WAF JS SDK (edge.sdk.awswaf.com/.../challenge.js) and calls AwsWafIntegration.fetch. A strong 'awswaf' marker would mark that source BLOCKED on every request. So bare 'awswaf' is now a weak marker (counts only on error statuses). AWS WAF challenge pages are still caught by strong markers: 'aws-waf-token', 'AwsWafIntegration.forceRefreshToken' (from sherlock), 'window.gokuProps' and the x-amzn-waf-action header. For the same reason, bare '_incapsula_resource' and 'ddos-guard' are weak, because normal Incapsula pages load /_Incapsula_Resource scripts. The strong markers for those vendors are 'Incapsula incident ID', '_Incapsula_Resource?CWUDNSAI', '<title>DDoS-Guard</title>' and 'check.ddos-guard.net'. The real page is the regression fixture tests/fixtures/http/normal_200_awswaf_sdk.html.

Additions beyond the spec: (1) body fingerprints are never applied to JSON documents, because APIs carry page titles such as 'Just a moment...' or 'Vercel Security Checkpoint' as data; (2) the final-URL login-wall rule applies only when the response was redirected (or to a 3xx Location), so a directly requested path such as GitHub user 'login' is not a wall; (3) the profile ttl is also a ceiling on a TTL the caller asks for, following P326 cond 7 'min(profile ttl, ...)' (the WP03 formula says 'requested or profile ttl'); (4) the Cloudflare server-header rule applies to 403, and to 503 only when cf-mitigated is set, so a down origin behind Cloudflare is not circuited; (5) HTTP 999 and Google /sorry/ pages map to blocked/challenge; (6) RequestsTransport never stores or replays cookies; (7) RequestInfo gains a trailing user_agent field; (8) the redirect loop stops at a 3xx that is itself classified (login wall, blockme), so the login page is never fetched.

Fixture provenance: research samples exist only for Cloudflare (challenge and block), Vercel, ISC blockme, CloudFront 503, the gov.br page and the HackerTarget, Criminal IP, IPQS, Etherscan, CheckPhish, hunter.how and TCU bodies. AWS WAF, PerimeterX, Incapsula, DDoS-Guard, Akamai and CloudFront-geo pages, plus the Leak-Lookup and ReceitaWS error bodies, are minimal reconstructions built from the maigret/sherlock marker strings and the documented error shapes. tests/fixtures/http/README.md lists each one. Over HttpClient the cap gate runs just before the first network send, so cache hits stay free.

A providers.register() made after the Runtime exists is therefore not seen by its HttpClient. HttpClient also accepts a callable, so the exact change is: in Runtime.__init__, pass providers=(lambda: self.providers) to HttpClient instead of providers=self.providers.

problems_found: Borrowed credentials: RequestsTransport used a plain requests.Session with trust_env=True, so requests attached ~/.netrc logins (Authorization: Basic) to any matching host. This broke the 'no borrowed cookies/sessions' rule; I reproduced it on a loopback server.

Host-check bypass through a parser differential: hop_check and ScopedHttp parse URLs with urllib.parse, but urllib3 sends to a different host for 'https://evil.test\\@api.example.test/' (urlsplit sees api.example.test, urllib3 connects to evil.test). Percent-encoded hosts behave the same way. A malicious redirect Location could reach an undeclared host.

A credential-bearing body was re-sent across origins: on a cross-origin 307/308 the POST body (form or JSON with apikey/token, or a registered secret) went to the new host. Only the credential headers were stripped.

ScopedHttp let per-call keywords override scope metadata. A module could pass charge_quota=False to skip quota, opsec='passive' from a LIGHT scope (the V3LUM/contact UA then went to a target), priority='seed' to spend the seed reserve, a later deadline to outrun the run deadline, its own cancel_event to bypass the kill switch, or min_interval=0 to drop its declared politeness.
Rule 5: get_json returned None (an absence) for any declared absent status, including 401/403/407/429/451/999/5xx, which mean 'could not verify'.

Circuit over-reach: a challenge reached through a redirect tripped the original host too, so a URL shortener died for the whole run. A bare keyless HTTP 403 also tripped the circuit, so one endpoint refusing keyless calls blocked keyed modules on the same host (for example the GitHub API's 403 rate limits).
Kill switch: Retry-After, backoff and politeness waits used clock.sleep, so a 15 s Retry-After ignored Ctrl+C/cancel for its full length (AR05/A7 require target traffic to stop within 2 s).

Missed challenge pages, found by running classify() over the research samples. The abuse.ch web UI 'Checking your browser' hCaptcha page (HTTP 200), the DomainTools 'Whois Lookup Captcha' page (200), the Netcraft JS challenge (200), the Facebook /__rd_verify_ challenge (403) and the Incapsula JS-challenge shape were all unclassified. The Reddit 'blocked by network security' page was also missed because its message sits after 190 KB of CSS, beyond the 64 KB scan.
Login-wall false positives: a module that requested a login URL, or queried an identity provider (login.* host) whose own redirects stay on that host, was classified login_wall.

Cache: the cache was chmod 0600 only after SQLite had created the -wal/-shm files with umask permissions (0644 with umask 022), so cached bodies were world-readable. Already-existing loose cache files were never tightened.
A profile ttl of 0 ('never cache this provider') was ignored whenever a module asked for a TTL.
A cache_if veto that raised crashed the request after the network call. On a cache hit that a module's own error marker rejected, the shared row was deleted for every other caller.
Sensitive providers: exceptions (raise_for_status/json) copied up to 500 characters of the raw body, so stealer computer names and IPs could reach exception text.
A caller-supplied contact UA (containing contact_email or contact_url) could reach unknown-tier or unregistered hosts (P326 cond 5).
The transport let OSError/ValueError (for example an unreadable ca_bundle path) escape as raw exceptions, and request timeouts carried reason_code 'error' instead of the canonical 'timeout'.
Redaction: key-like parameters at the start of free text or form bodies ('apikey=...&x', echoed in error texts) were not masked; only ?/&/;/# contexts were.

Minor items: there was no cap on per-call retries. On a cache hit without redirects the module got back the redacted (and possibly normalised) URL instead of its own. The Connector's connection counter was not thread-safe. The notice fragment and the http.py header lacked the upstream commit ids that the A6 notice rules ask for.

Design choice for reviewers: Quad9 (RFC 8484 wire format) builds and parses messages with dnspython's dns.message but sends them through the http object the Resolver receives, not dns.query.https. This keeps the core DoH scope's proxy, TLS verification, redaction and disclosure ledger on that traffic.

Design choice for reviewers: besides transport errors, 5xx and 429, failover also happens on intermediary refusals (401/403/407/408/451) and on HTTP-200 bodies that are not a DoH answer (challenge or captive-portal page). It never happens on a DNS answer (NOERROR, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, REFUSED). Other 4xx give SERVFAIL without failover.

Design choice for reviewers: domain noise matching stops at the PSL registrable domain, as in v1. Hosts under PSL private suffixes (x.akamaiedge.net, buckets under s3.<region>.amazonaws.com, tenant.azurewebsites.net, evil.github.io) are therefore their own registrable domains and are investigated, not treated as noise.

problems_found: dns.py: failed over to the next resolver on HTTP 401/403/407/451 and on challenge pages. This breaks P029 cond 1, the WP04 spec and the frozen MODULE_GUIDE, which all say failover happens only on transport errors, 5xx and 429. tests/test_dns_hardening.py asserted the wrong behaviour.

dns.py: OfflineError and the HTTP layer's per-run host short-circuit (Blocked, reason_code 'circuit') were counted as resolver failures. In offline mode this opened the circuit breaker after 3 uncached names, so later cached answers were skipped and gave a spurious SERVFAIL.

dns.py: the internal-resolver check let public resolvers pass as 'internal', and internal is the only resolver allowed at TLP:RED. Examples that passed: a trailing-dot host (https://dns.google./resolve), a subdomain (https://mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com), IPv6 or IPv4-mapped literals ([2001:4860:4860::8888], [::ffff:8.8.8.8]). A misconfiguration could leak RED queries.
dns.py: config_errors repeated rejected DoH URLs word for word, so credentials or token query values could reach logs and doctor output.
dns.py: the resolver's Comment/EDE text went into DnsAnswer.error with no length limit and with control characters (ANSI escapes, newlines): a terminal-injection risk.
dns.py: wildcard() returned False for NOERROR/NODATA zones. The spec says False only when both probes are NXDOMAIN, and P029 cond 10 needs NODATA zones to be told apart from real records.

datasets.py: fetch_text, fetch_json and fetch_lines shared one memo entry per path. Confirmed: fetch_json after fetch_text returned a str, and fetch_lines returned the same str. The memo and the SHA memo also keyed only on mtime+size.

datasets.py: a non-zip body for a zip dataset raised zipfile.BadZipFile, deeply nested JSON raised RecursionError, and OSError from mkstemp or the write escaped as-is. All confirmed: the module crashed instead of getting a DatasetError with the previous copy served as stale.
datasets.py: the HTML/anti-bot sniff skipped expect='text', so an error page could replace a text dataset.

datasets.py, local copies and indexes: fetch_json on a corrupt local copy raised a bare ValueError; index() let csv.Error and RecursionError escape. Lines and json indexes of the same dataset version shared one SQLite file. Read-only SQLite connections leaked, half-built index temp files survived failures, and index temp files were world-readable until chmod.
datasets.py: bundled_text, bundled_path and bundled_exists accepted '../' and absolute names, so reads could escape v3lum/data.
datasets.py: fetch(name, url) with a registered name downloaded from any other URL under that name. This breaks the licence/terms/pin provenance and turns ctx.data into a download-anything client.

datasets.py: update(accept_new=True) installed a changed active dataset without its diff summary being shown first. The spec says such a dataset is accepted only after the diff summary. Active datasets could also be refreshed during a scan (A6: never mid-engagement).

noise.py: the licence check was a leaky deny-list. Fragments licensed 'CC BY SA 4.0', 'Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike', ODbL, EUPL, MPL, CC BY-ND, 'proprietary' or 'unknown' were accepted as bundled data, but A6 is an allow-list.
orgprofile.py: no file-mode check (P378 cond 1: 0600). A world-writable profile let any local user mark domains txt_verified/attested and unlock own-asset and per-person modules.

orgprofile.py, smaller gaps: a top-level 'name' key (JSON style, used by WP01's tests/test_rule_fixtures.py) was flagged unknown and dropped. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses were not matched against own CIDRs. A configured org_profile_path that does not exist gave an empty profile with no error.
fixes_applied: dns.py, failover: _FAILOVER_STATUS is now {408, 429} plus 500-599. Every other non-200 status gives SERVFAIL marked 'could not verify' for that query, with no failover and no circuit count. A 200 body classified 'blocked' (challenge/login/geo page) is a refusal; other bodies that are not a DoH answer are treated as corrupt transfers and fail over. Blocked/AuthRequired exceptions are refusals. The module docstring was updated to match the guide.

dns.py, offline and circuit: OfflineError now skips that resolver without counting toward the circuit, so cached answers keep working. A host the HTTP layer has short-circuited for the run is skipped like an open resolver circuit.

dns.py, public resolvers: added is_public_doh_host() (in __all__). It matches public DoH domains and their subdomains on label boundaries, strips a trailing dot, and checks public resolver networks for IP literals, including IPv4-mapped ones. _validate_internal uses it and survives URLs that cannot be parsed.

dns.py, error text: rejected URLs are reported as scheme://host only. _short() and _comment() strip control characters and cap the length, so resolver text arrives as one bounded line. _bad_body() evicts non-DNS bodies from caches that could not refuse to store them.
dns.py, wildcard: wildcard()/WildcardInfo return None with nodata=True for NOERROR/NODATA zones. That result is a real DNS answer, so it is cached; could-not-verify results still are not.

tests/test_dns_hardening.py, new tests: failover on 502/504/408; no failover on 401/403/407/451 or a challenge page served with 200; a 503 challenge page still fails over; short-circuited host is skipped; Blocked/AuthRequired are refusals; offline mode never trips the circuit; more internal-URL rejection cases; is_public_doh_host; Comment sanitising; no credential echo; NODATA wildcard. The old test that expected failover on a challenge page was corrected.
datasets.py, memo: keyed per reader kind and per file stamp (inode, size, mtime, ctime). The SHA memo uses the same stamp.

datasets.py, refresh errors: a corrupt zip, deep JSON, OSError, UnicodeError and csv errors during a refresh now raise DatasetError, so the previous copy is served as stale. mkstemp failure is wrapped too, and temp files are always cleaned up. The HTML sniff now covers expect='text'.

datasets.py, local copies and indexes: fetch_json on a corrupt local copy raises DatasetError. index() wraps csv, recursion and unicode errors. SQLite index file names include format and column. Read-only connections are closed. Index temp files are created 0600 with O_EXCL and removed on failure.
datasets.py, bundled names: _bundled_ref() rejects absolute paths, drive letters, '..' and NUL. bundled_exists() returns False for such names; subdirectories such as noise/core.json still work.
datasets.py, URL provenance: fetch() refuses a URL that differs from the registered one with a DatasetError, and makes no request. Calls with the registered URL, the old positional form, still work.

datasets.py, active datasets: update(accept_new=True) stages the copy and returns needs_accept with the diff summary unless a staged copy exists or a matching reviewed expect_sha256 is given. update() refuses active datasets while in_scan. ReDoS in entities.refang(), which detect runs on whole pasted texts: the pre-existing rule r'\s+dot\s+' is quadratic on whitespace runs (40k spaces took 6 s; 1 MB would hang). The COORDINATES normalizer regex r'\s*[,; ]\s*' was also super-linear.
redacted_value() raised ValueError for an empty JWT, secret or telegram_bot_token value. It is called on persist and export paths and must never raise.
